transcript: Operator: We will begin the quarterly call. CEO: New customer commitments increased across several regions, and the number of projects entering implementation was higher than last quarter. We now expect full-year growth of 9% to 11%, up from our previous range of 6% to 8%. CFO: The range reflects the orders currently in hand and the renewal activity we have observed. Analyst: Does the increase depend on one customer? CEO: No, the improvement is broad-based. We are confident in the higher range, while recognizing that project start dates can shift.

CEO: Conversations with customers have become more constructive. We expect activity to improve gradually over the coming periods, although the timing will vary by market. We are not providing a numeric forecast today. CFO: The pipeline is healthier than it was earlier in the year, but not every planned project has received final approval. Analyst: Can you estimate how quickly the improvement will translate into sales? CEO: We cannot give a precise timetable. Our view is directionally better, but still measured.

CFO: Customer demand remains close to the level we have seen throughout the year. Our full-year sales outlook is unchanged at $620 million to $660 million. CEO: Renewals are steady, and new project activity is mixed across customer groups. We do not see a reason to raise or lower the range. Analyst: Has the outlook changed since the previous call? CFO: No. The assumptions and numerical range remain the same.

CEO: Cancellations increased and customer approvals slowed in the final weeks of the quarter. We now expect annual revenue to fall 12% to 16%, compared with our earlier expectation of growth between 1% and 3%. CFO: We have reduced our forecast to reflect weaker orders and lower renewal rates. Analyst: Could the second half recover enough to meet the old outlook? CEO: We do not expect that. The current environment is materially weaker than we anticipated, and our revised range reflects that deterioration.

CEO: Some customers are extending decision timelines, and we expect a modest slowdown in new project starts. Existing service activity remains steady, but growth is likely to be lower than it was in the first half. We are not issuing a numerical forecast. CFO: We will continue to review the order pipeline as approvals come through. Analyst: Is this a sharp drop or a gradual change? CEO: Our current expectation is a gradual softening, though we cannot yet say how long it will last.
